3. The defendant appeared in the suit and filed written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint stating; inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner; that the suit is barred by law of limitation and the allegation for causing loss amounting to Tk.1,56,569.38 is not only unspecific also without any legal basis and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 7. Drawing our attention to the plaint of the suit as well as Article 36 of the Limitation Act, 1908, Mr. A. K. M. Shafiuddin, the learned Advocate submits that the cause of action for the suit arose firstly on 13.9.82 but the suit was filed on 6.7.1986 and in that view of the matter the suit was clearly barred by law of limitation but the Courts below having failed to appreciate this simple question of law and thereby most illegally decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff and as such the impugned judgments of 2 (two) Courts below are liable to be set-aside. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr. Tufailur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff- opposite party supports the impugned judgments of two Courts below which were according to him just, correct and proper. The learned Advocate in the course of his argument after placing the deposition of PWs. and the averments of the plaint submits that the suit is not barred by law of limitation inasmuch as it is apparent from the plaint that the last cause of action for filing the suit is on 25.8.1985. He next relying on the decision reported in 7 MLR 132 submits that from the averments of the plaint clearly show that how the plaintiff suffered the damage or loss by the defendant in details and as such the question of interference for want of cause of action does not arise at all. 

 9. Mr. Tufailur Rahman, the learned Advocate finally submits that the petitioner was employed under a service contract with the plaintiff-mills and in that view of the matter the provision of section 36 of the Limitation Act will not applicable in this Case. 

 11. Both the Courts below on assessment of the evidence on record arrived at a concurrent finding that the suit was not barred by law of limitation and the plaintiff by adducing sufficient evidence has been succeeded to prove that the defendant-petitioner with malafide intention caused financial loss amounting to Tk.I,56,569.38 to the plaintiff jute mills. The Courts below hl also held that the question of limitation is a close chapter in view of the fact that the defendant-petitioner had raised the question of limitation before the trial Court in an' application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and became unsuccessful and against which unsuccessful defendant did not file any appeal. 

 12. The reasons given by the Courts below on the point of limitation are not sustainable either in law or on facts inasmuch as the proposition of law is well settled that the question of limitation in a suit is a mixed question of law and fact which can be decided only at the trial on taking evidence. 

 13. Now let us look at the more important question whether the suit was barred by limitation. In this connection a portion of the plaint is required to be referred to for having a better view of the dispute in question. A b portion of the plaint reads as follows: 

 14. We have already noticed that the defendant-petitioner was appointed by the plaintiff for purchasing raw jute for and on behalf of the plaintiff-Adamjee Jute Mills Corporation and the authority of the Jute Mills on assessment of the purchased raw jute found that the defendant caused a financial loss amounting to Tk. 1,56,569.38 to the plaintiff-opposite party and thereupon, the authority of the Jute Mills brought charge against him and finally dismissed him from service against which the petitioner unsuccessfully moved Title suit No. 147 of 1983. Thus, we find there is a good deal of substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the suit, which was filed on 6.7.86 for the recovery of an alleged loss caused by misfeasance, malfeasance or nonfeasance in the year 1981-82 and discovered on 26.10.82, was well beyond the 2 (two) years limitation period, prescribed by Article 36 of the Limitation Act, 1908. Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case vis-a-vis the provisions of Article 36 of the Limitation Act, 1908, we are of the view that the suit is barred by law of limitation. 

 16. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are not agree with the learned Advocate for the respondent-opposite party that section 36 of the Limitation Act, 1908 is not applicable in the instant case. The decision cited by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party is distinguishable on facts.
